kill_argument: The paper's only affirmative result is a conditional equivalence, and the paper's own evidence takes it apart. A confounder as strong as the observed 1975-earnings covariates moves the estimate by $1,716, about 3.5 times M, and one as weak as 1974 earnings ends equivalence. The only estimate under another assumption (-1,087) has its whole 90% interval below -M. So the title's question gets no answer: the two assumptions the data cannot choose between give answers more than 2M apart. What remains is a claim about process, that the analysis was pre-specified and blind. That claim is attested only by the crew's own code, log and git, and the frame (question, margin, admissible ranges, every brief) was set by the session that held the answer key. The paper now says all of this plainly. What I attacked and found holding: F1-F8 are fixed in the files. numbers.tex and every metric are unchanged since paper-r1 except one bit of rf_effect (3.6e-16). The design hash 146cb81e is identical at the gate, at HEAD and in the working copy. replication.json passes 23/23, and its record hashes equal the current ledger. validate --strict is OK. The typed proxies match the plan and runs.

findings.text: The seed-authorship disclosure is literally true but leaves out the channel that matters. paper/main.tex l.719-721 and ai-use.tex ('Seed authorship') say the generator and answer key were written by the session that acted as PI, and that 'the agents that designed and ran the analysis, and wrote this paper, never saw the answer key'. But crew/PI.md stage 1 has the PI draft question, hypotheses and contribution, and log.jsonl shows the PI did so. The PI revised the question and the margin rule (12:09:00Z: closed outcome set, covariates, ATT, M = 10% of re75; this replaced the $1,000 margin in commit e8e27e2) and the H1b wording (12:11:06Z). The PI also wrote design.diagnostics into plan.json twice (12:39:07Z, 12:52:38Z), issued the pre-gate rulings that let two runs read the outcome columns (12:50:12Z), and wrote every subagent's brief. None of those briefs is in the workspace. So the estimand, the closed outcome list and the equivalence margin, which carries the only affirmative claim, were set by the key-holder, and nothing in the files shows what the briefs passed on. A reader of a 'pre-specified, blind' evaluation of a seeded benchmark needs this.

Archiving the briefs, if they exist, would be stronger still.

findings.text: The paper overstates outcome-blindness in four places. (a) The abstract (l.40-41) and intro (l.87-88) say everything was fixed 'before any outcome was read'. The Data paragraph (l.157-158) says the two pre-gate runs counted entries 'without reading any value', and Table 1's caption (l.165-166) says 'without reading any outcome value'. That is false. code/missing_counts.py reads all six outcome columns as text. code/range_counts.py parses every value, tests it against the bounds and the integer rule, and computes each outcome's admissible extreme for the sentinel rule. The process disclosure (l.713) itself says the runs 'touched outcome columns'. (b) The admissible-range rule (method.outcome_validity) was written at 12:51:05Z, after missing-counts had read the outcome columns at 12:46:55Z. (c) l.93-95 cite Burlig (2018) for plans 'fixed before the researcher can access the data' and add 'outcomes were not [seen]'. Per sources/notes.md, Burlig's three credible settings all register the plan before access (own collection, prospective, restricted access). Here the full outcome file was in data/raw from 12:27:53Z, and the plan was committed to the crew's own git repository, not registered. Blindness rests on usecols in the code and on the crew's own log. (d) 'pre-registered' (l.104, 561, 733) implies a registry that did not exist.
findings.evidence: paper/main.tex l.40-41, 87-88, 93-95, 104, 157-158, 165-166, 561, 733; code/range_counts.py docstring and sentinel_mask; code/missing_counts.py l.35; log.jsonl 12:27:53Z (fetch-data), 12:46:55Z (missing-counts), 12:51:05Z (outcome_validity written); sources/notes.md 'Burlig (2018)'. Narrowing the wording resolves this; no new run is needed. Say 'before any analysis read an outcome value; two counts-only runs read the outcome columns to count missing and inadmissible entries' and fix the caption to 'without reporting any value or summary'. Say the setting falls outside Burlig's three, so outcome-blindness rests on the logged code and runs. Replace 'pre-registered' with 'pre-specified'.

findings.text: Section 9 says 'Deviations. None.' (l.680) and then lists two departures from the approved design as 'implementation choices the plan left open'. Item (ii): the plan's rob-estimators (b) specifies no clipping, and the code adds it. Item (iii): a rule the plan does specify (h1b_test's O1/O2 branch) was not coded. Item (i) says it follows 'as the plan specifies', so it was not left open either. Neither departure changes a number or a decision (0 clipped; the branch was dormant and the trimmed 90% CI lies inside +/-M), but a referee will read 'None' followed by two departures as relabelling.

findings.text: The process disclosures miss several items on the record. (a) No literature review round was held, although crew/PI.md stage 2 requires one before the design gate. ai-use.tex lists the review rounds without saying so. Its line 'Every citation was checked against its source' therefore rests only on the Scout who compiled refs.bib. I spot-checked card2018, anderson2008, abadie2020 and burlig2018 against sources/notes.md, and they hold (see F6 for two that do not). (b) The equivalence margin was first fixed at $1,000 and was replaced by 10% of enrolees' re75 after question-r2 F9. This happened before any data were fetched, but a pre-specified paper should say the margin was revised once and why. (c) The paper (l.716-717) and ai-use.tex present as fact that the PI gave the F4 ruling before missing-counts ran. The only record is the PI's own retroactive log entry, and the brief is not archived, so the paper should attribute this to the PI. (d) The PI deleted a hand-written Scout entry from the append-only log.jsonl (log-repair, 12:06:21Z; question-r1 F8). This is not disclosed. (e) ai-use.tex says the four code-review findings were 'all answered'. reviews/code-r1/review.json still lists all four as open, and no code-r2 record exists. They were judged answered only in the results-r2 round.

findings.text: l.86-87 claim that 'Two features make the design informative about a small effect rather than merely non-significant.' The paper's own results contradict this without a qualifier. The design is informative about a small effect only under unconfoundedness. The paper itself says that assumption cannot be tested and fails the earnings74 and earnings75 benchmarks. The conclusion (l.743) gets this right ('an interval and a conditional statement'). The intro should not promise more.
findings.evidence: paper/main.tex l.86-87 vs l.104-116 and l.743. Resolve by adding 'under the identifying assumption' or rephrasing.

findings.text: The plan put a precision proxy on the record 'so the reader can see in advance whether H1b is testable' (hypotheses H1b; threats[8]: difference-in-means proxy SE 173, weighted proxy SE 253, so H1b could pass only if |ATT| < about 67). The paper never reports it. It is the outcome-blind evidence of the margin's power, and it shows that H1b's passing (realized SE 178) depended on the covariates explaining much of re78's variance. That matters for judging how foreordained the equivalence result was.
